summary: Large language model (LLM) agents typically append raw tool outputs to their context. Over multi-step interactions, long and noisy observations incur substantial context overhead and dilute the agent's attention to task-relevant information.
takeaways: Coca-Cola compresses tool observations into latent tokens and embeds them into the input embedding space of the agent.

Experiments with web-search agents on four QA benchmarks and two model families show that Coca-Cola reduces the agent's token consumption by 70.01%-89.24% and end-to-end runtime by 24.45%-55.97%, while consistently improving task performance.
In this work, we challenge the prevailing assumption that agents must consume tool observations as explicit text tokens.
